Calculations use the cutter diameter, number of teeth, cutting speed, and cutting feed, difference work-piece material and tool material should be chosen based on the specific cutting conditions. Materials have rated surface speeds for a given type of cutter. The harder the material the slower the speed.

Feed Rate is the speed at which the cutter engages the part and is typically measured in units/minute.

Spindle Speed is the rotational frequency of the spindle of the machine, measured in revolutions per minute (RPM). The preferred speed is determined by working backward from the desired surface speed (sfm or m/min) and incorporating the diameter (of workpiece or cutter).

Formula:
RPM = (12 * SFM) / (PI * CD)
RPM = 3.82 * SFM / CD
IPR = Ft x NT 
IPM = Ft x NT x RPM
IPM = IPR x rpm

Where:
RPM - Spindle Speed
Ft - Feed/Tooth, Chip Load/Tooth
SFM - Surface Speed
IPM - Feed Rate
CD - Cutter Diameter
NT - Cutter Number of Teeth
IPR - Cutting Feed

Distance attenuation is defined as the way in which a sound level [dB] reduces as a listener moves away from a sound source. As sound travels from the source, the area over which the sound is spread increases like ripples on a pond. This means that the same amount of acoustic energy is dispersed over a greater area, and as a result the sound level at any position on this area reduces as the distance from the source is increased.

Sound attenuation describes how the SPL [dB] changes with increasing distance from the sound source. 

The sound attenuation formula is as follows:

SPL₂ = SPL₁ - 20 * log (D₂ / D₁)

where:
SPL₁ - Sound Pressure Level [dB] at point 1
SPL₂ - Sound Pressure Level [dB] at point 2
D₁ - Distance from the sound source to point 1
D₂ - Distance from the sound source to point 2

Bonjour uses industry standard IP protocols to allow devices to automatically discover each other without the need to enter IP addresses or configure DNS servers. The Bonjour-Browser in iNet scans the connected local network for Bonjour services, detecting any hardware that ist connected via the Bonjour protocol (for instance computer, router, printer, …) and any software running Bonjour services, e. g. iTunes or Filemaker.
